Nur Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Strękowo, Poland

Demolished. Nur, granted Chełmno town rights before 1416 and made a royal town in 1526, had a small Jewish community from the early 18th century - just 10 among 597 Christians by 1807, growing to 299 (of 813) by 1860 and about 400 by 1921. In 1940, Nur's Jews were relocated to the Ciechanów Ghetto, later deported to Treblinka in 1942. This cemetery, likely established mid-19th century, was enclosed with a concrete fence before the war (partly surviving as the western boundary); tombstones were used to build town foundations during and after WWII.
